clue.text: Easy to carry, wine and beer bachelor brought in

parts.note: port is a fortified Portuguese wine

indicators.note: the bachelor's letter is brought into the middle of the beer word

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone choosing drinks to carry home, with a bachelor bringing the beer in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portable can be picked up and moved about with little effort, which is what easy to carry means.

clue.text: Piece of glass left in section of door

parts.note: a pane is a single sheet of glass in a window or door

explanation.surface: A glazier fitting a pane on the left-hand part of a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a flat rectangular piece forming part of a door, a standard carpentry term.

clue.text: Soft cheese actor spread with it

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters of the two words are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor smearing a soft cheese with something, perhaps on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft, mild Italian whey cheese, an example of the category named.

definitions.note: read as something that numbs, not a figure

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
aesthetic means concerned with beauty and good taste

explanation.surface: A music critic's description of a tasteful song or dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count or a song; read it as NUM-ber, a thing that makes you numb. 'on' just places the article above the rest in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic is a drug that deadens feeling, so it is literally a thing that numbs, the cryptic sense of the word.

clue.text: Celebrity raised in outskirts of Limoges, French city

indicators.note: in places the turned-up celebrity word between the two outskirt letters
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of the place name are used
in a down entry, raised means the word is written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a name is a famous person, as in a big name

explanation.surface: A celebrity being brought up on the edge of Limoges, a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Limoges looks like the city wanted, but it only supplies its edge letters; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Mans is a city in north-west France, famous for its 24-hour motor race.

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A sharp team of police detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid taste is sour and biting, so acid works as a synonym of sharp.

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone dancing in their study alongside a woman called Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' meaning to study or memorise is an old sense, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance in which people follow each other in single file.

indicators.note: working means the letters are being worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Can you put up with it when your work takes you far from home?
explanation.definitionFit: Distant describes something remote, a long way off, so it means far away.

clue.text: MC in saloon crashing with bus, losing this?

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters of the words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A compère driving a saloon car smashes into a bus and fears for his insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the scene, but only 'losing this?' defines: a driver who crashes forfeits this insurance discount.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist's insurance discount for claim-free years is forfeited after an accident, which is what crashing into a bus would cost.

parts.note: a brain is a clever person, an egghead
teas are cups of tea, drinks
taken as written, the dropped-aitch form of her

explanation.surface: A clever man having tea with a woman and finding it hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle that taxes the mind is a kind of problem, here a specific example.

indicators.note: vandalised means damaged and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Yobs damaging a plant in a park.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, an example of a plant.

indicators.note: returning means the word for once more is read backwards

parts.note: again means once more
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for an artist

explanation.surface: An artist returning yet again and falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the famous waterfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the name of the great waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Ostentatiously stylish, like hotel described by pilot

indicators.note: described in the sense of drawn round, so the pilot word goes round the others

parts.note: to fly is to pilot an aircraft
as can mean like, as in white as snow
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pilot calling a hotel showily glamorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described' is used in its geometric sense, as when a circle is drawn round something.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashy means showy and attention-seeking in style, a direct synonym.

parts.note: an earful is a telling-off

explanation.surface: A woman scared of being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets F above the rest in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearful means full of fear, a plain synonym of being afraid.

parts.note: a fan cools the air

explanation.surface: A cooler temperature helps a mother give birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivers' only links the wordplay to the definition, though it fits the birth scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, so it is a straight synonym of baby.

parts.note: L stands for the pound, from Latin libra
the ready is British slang for cash, as in short of the ready

explanation.surface: A list of money items, a pound and some cash, tallied so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ready' (or 'readies') is British slang for money in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time, which is what thus far means.

clue.text: Slight earthquake in heart of Castries, revolutionary capital

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so the two central letters of the place name are taken
revolutionary means turned round, so the capital's name is read backwards

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A minor quake shakes Castries, the capital of St Lucia, amid revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Castries is the capital of St Lucia, but here only its middle letters TR matter; the capital whose letters are used is ROME, which 'revolutionary' turns into EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a small shaking of the ground, the term for a minor earthquake.

clue.text: Judge a Republican, one using his teeth

parts.note: a biter is one who bites

explanation.surface: A Republican judge who bites, perhaps a ferocious courtroom figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter settles disputes, so the word means a judge or referee.

definitions.meaning: describing weather that is chilly and harsh, or a bare windswept place
the name of a small silvery European river fish

explanation.surface: Raw fish served cold, like sushi.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak describes harsh, cold, exposed conditions, and is also the name of a small freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Almost missing header at the start

indicators.note: the header is the first letter, so the word for almost loses its opening letter

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A footballer nearly scored but missed a header right at the start of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' looks like football; it is the first letter of NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means at or near the beginning of a period, which is what at the start means.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone performing songs in Tokyo, beautifully.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, a particular way of singing.

clue.text: Dutchman errs, sprinkling on fine condiment

indicators.note: on means the rearranged letters come after, as if placed upon, the letter for fine

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: sprinkling scatters things about, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dutchman making a mistake, sprinkling sauce on something fine.
explanation.definitionFit: French mustard is a mild Dijon-style mustard, an example of a condiment eaten with food.

definitions.meaning: to be fond of or take pleasure in something
similar, matching, as in a pair of the same kind

explanation.definitionFit: To like something is to enjoy it, and as an adjective like means similar or matching, so corresponding.

clue.text: Two kings on board a majestic old flagship

indicators.note: on board means the kings are carried inside the other words, like passengers aboard a ship

parts.note: royal means kingly, majestic
R (rex) and K (as in chess) are both abbreviations for king

explanation.surface: Two monarchs boarding a grand ship of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ark Royal is the name of several British Royal Navy flagships, the last an aircraft carrier retired in 2011.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Royal Navy ships named Ark Royal served as fleet flagships, so the name fits an old flagship.
